rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A is about a missing onProgress/toast callback during the PPTX image-fetch phase in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts; Finding B is about a line break in packages/documentation/slides/themes-and-layouts.md making "Modern Writer" look like two themes. Different files, different problems — fixing either leaves the other standing.

panel.finding_key: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts::no progress toast during the pptx image-fetch phase
panel.summary: No progress toast during the PPTX image-fetch phase
panel.evidence: `exportPptx` fetches every unique image (Step 2, lines 154-167) before the first `onProgress?.(0, slideTotal, 'slides')` at line 272. Because `updateExportToast` only creates the toast on the first callback, a deck with many images shows no progress toast at all while the (potentially slowest) network phase runs — only the header spinner. The PDF path calls onProgress before its asset resolution comparably; here a `images` phase callback would match the documented 'mirroring the PDF path' claim in pptx-actions.ts:83-85.
